body: The Neo-Baroque-style building was built during the British colonial era to house the Legislative Council of Ceylon, and was an idea of Sir Henry McCallum. The building was opened on 29 January 1930. In 1972, the National State Assembly convened in the building until 1977, when it was renamed the Parliament of Sri Lanka. Parliament then moved out to new complex and the building then became home to the Presidential Secretariat. It faces the sea in Colombo fort area and it is built in Neo-Boroque style
title: Great monument in Colombo

body: The old Parliament Building is a remarkable Colonial architecture having a political history and stands in front of the sea. It is located in the heart of of Colombo Fort, this architectural marvel is a unique building in Sri Lanka.It is now the office of the President. Therefore, there is high security employed and declared as high security area. The sea is just after the Gall road that runs in front of it. Therefore no parking or stoppage of vehicles are allowed and you have to reach there by walking. The garden / front area land is covered by high iron fence and you are not allowed inside but only see and appreciate the building from little far. People allowed in are only on appointment or to attend a function by invitation. It is a beauty of Colombo. And the old colonial building with European architecture is ionic. The parliament was shifted to Sri Jayawardenapura after new building was constructed. Some State functions takes place here such as Sworn of the Presidents, Foreign head of state Politician’s visits, Presidents address /meetings with concerned parties etc.You may take photos from outside the fenced area near the Galle road. Old Parliament Building shows the Old charm which was a symbol of the past where the venue for the preservation of the rights of the people, respect the legacy, history took place in the past. The hotels; Galadari, Hilton, Kingsbury, Shangrila, ITC, Taj Samudra and Galleface Hotel are in close proximity. Nearby the Treasury, Ministry of Finance, Departments of National Planning, External Resources are located. The world trade center Colombo is close by.
title: Remarkable Colonial Old Parliament Building Having Political History Stands Scenic Seafront.

body: It's a beautiful colonial building built by the British & declared open on 29th January 1930, located on Lotus Road, Colombo Fort, in close proximity of the Galadari, Hilton, Kingsbury, Shangrila, ITC, Taj Samudra & Galleface Hotels. Behind it the Treasury, Ministry of Finance, Departments of National Planning, External Resources are located. The world trade center, Colombo, Bank of Ceylon, The Central Bank, Naval HQ, former Dutch Hospital, Colombo Port, Ministry of Defence & Queen's House the Presidential Palace are located in the surrounding areas. The building boats of majestic neo-baroque style architecture was declared open by the British Governor Sir Herbert Stanley. It housed the Ceylon State Council in 1931.It was declared as the Parliament of Sri Lanka in 1977 and functioned as the Parliament until 1983. Currently it houses the Presidential Secretariat at which many distinguished state guests and business delegations are hosted. Both the internal as well as external architecture is uniquely well designed.

body: The Neo-Baroque-style building was built during the British colonial era to house the Legislative Council of Ceylon. It was built on an idea of Sir Henry McCallum, which led to a proposal made by a committee to construct the new building for the Secretariat, Council Chamber and Government offices on reclaimed land at the northern end of Galle Face' were accepted by the Government in 1920.. Woodson was responsible for the design of the building. The initial estimate of Rs 400,000 for the scheme was later revised by the Public Works Advisory Board to Rs 450,000, taking into account the extra expenses involved

body: Being itself a grand "colonial building" with tall pillars all around on the sides, this building also has great counterparts (some well-preserved "beautiful" buildings from the colonial era, but others modern high-rises of the present time) nearby like The Kingsbury (must be the "greatest" hotel of Colombo just from the look of the building!) and the big white Presidential Palace; also while in the area, be sure to check out the lovely 'Old Lighthouse' just about a five-minute walk to the north from this building (I was especially delighted by the little "charming" street lined with lovely well-maintained buildings leading to the Lighthouse from the east side; being in that street was like almost "stepping back in time", and yes I'm sure there are more streets like that one in this area with "quite a few" well-preserved colonial-era buildings).You can either come up here from Galle Face Green (with the seaside promenade so "lively" with vendors' tents beside the Green) which is just about a 15-minute walk south of here, or take the bus to Colombo Fort (the city's "main station" for both trains & buses) and head west from there for about 15 to 20 minutes although that's not as straightforward a way as heading straight up north along the promenade beside Galle Face Green.

body: The Old Parliament building stands in all its neo-baroque glory overlooking the sea at the north end of the Galle Face Green. It is worth looking at as a stately reminder of many years of Sri Lanka's vibrant history. It served as the Parliament building until a new Parliament complex was constructed in 1983. It was built in the British Colonial era and is steeped in history. A very pleasant walk, especially in the early evening, is along the Galle Face Green from the Galle Face Hotel at the southern end to the Old Parliament building at the other.

body: The Old Parliament Building houses the Presidential Secretariat of Sri Lanka. The Letter of credence of incoming ambassadors and high commissioners are accepted by the President here. This Neo-Baroque-style building was built during the British colonial era to house the Legislative Council of Ceylon. It was inaugurated on January 29, 1930 by Governor Sir Herbert Stanley. It houses the island's legislature for 53 years until the New Parliament Complex was opened at Sri Jayawardenepura in 1983. The building faces the sea and is close to the Presidential house. Though not open for tourists one can see the building from the outside.
title: The old parliament building

body: Stately and British, this structure, with a lovely green patch in front, is today referred to as the President's office as the Parliament does not function here anymore. The Galadari hotel overlooks this building, at the corner of the Galle Face Road, facing the ocean.

title: Presidential Office
body: This majestic building in Galle face was turned into the Presidential Office after the Parliament was shifted to Sri Jayawardenapura.

title: Stately old building!
